newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gold starts firmer in Europe, silver rebounds.
newsitem.headline: Gold starts firmer in Europe, silver rebounds.

text.p: Gold opened firmer and silver held overnight gains in early Wednesday European trading.
Dealers expected prices to settle into ranges as the market consolidated gold's recent slide to three-year lows.
Gold opened at $368.70/369.10 an ounce, up from $367.60/$368.10 at the London close.
One dealer at a big Swiss bank saw a range of $367.50 to $370.50 today as the dollar eased.
He said he had not spotted any big producer selling so far.
Silver rose to $4.78/$4.80 from $4.70/$4.72, but traders said the mood was volatile.
"This can change very quickly and we could be right back to $4.60," one Swiss dealer said, suggesting hedge funds were behind the move. "It is always a casino with silver."
Traders said the mood for precious metals remained bearish, but added uncertainty about Europe's single currency project could help support prices if currency markets become more turbulent.
Other metals were little changed. Platinum started at $371.75/$372.75, up from $370.50/$371.50, while palladium firmed 25 cents to $114.50/$115.50.
